subject: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: legal@crosscloud.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization

Hi Jared / CrossCloud legal team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the integration looks promising and the technical team is aligned. Before we move to an SOW and procurement, legal asked I coordinate a short clause harmonization so we can identify the narrow list of exceptions your team needs vs. Redwood’s standard MSA/DPA/SOW templates.

I've attached a short mapping request and our current MSA/DPA/SOW (clean + markups). Could you: 1) return a one-page summary listing the partner clauses you require (indemnity, audit scope, IP carveouts, data residency, subcontractors, breach notification SLA); and 2) attach your redlined MSA/DPA? That will help us run a quick trade-off analysis.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed 7/2: receive your redlines + one-page ask list
- Thu 7/3: 30-min legal sync if needed
- Fri 7/4: motion to finalize term sheet and issue PO timeline

Important context from Redwood:
- We aim to keep liability caps to a commercial multiple of fees (typical: 1–2x) rather than open-ended indemnities.
- DPA changes are negotiable but we need clear data processing boundaries and any requests for audit must be scoped.
- We cannot accept reverse-engineering or perpetual source-code escrow obligations.

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood_MSA_v4_clean.pdf (attachment)
- Redwood_DPA_v2_track_changes.pdf (attachment)
- Redwood_SOW_template.docx (attachment)

If you'd prefer to skip the call and exchange a summary, happy either way.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Jared Miles <jm@crosscloud.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@crosscloud.com, procurement@crosscloud.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization

Rishi —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attaching our redlined MSA and a short memo highlighting the three priority items from our side:
1) Indemnity / IP: We need general indemnity for third-party IP claims and a carve-out for open-source that we ship as part of integration.
2) Liability cap: we prefer a 3x fees cap for first 12 months of the SOW while the integration is in initial production.
3) Audit & data access: we want the right to conduct a vendor security review (once annually) and limited access to logs for joint-support troubleshooting; we can't accept vendor-hosted full-sys audits.

A few attachments: CrossCloud_MSA_redline.docx (redline), CrossCloud_DPA_track_changes.pdf (notes). Procurement copied here; they ask whether Redwood can accept their standard PO terms (short form) or whether you need a full contract signature.

Happy to do a 30-minute call if it speeds things up — Wed afternoon works for our counsel.

Best,
Jared Miles
Head of Business Ops
CrossCloud Inc.

---
Attachment stubs: CrossCloud_MSA_redline.docx, CrossCloud_DPA_track_changes.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jared Miles <jm@crosscloud.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization

Jared — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. I skimmed the highlights and flagged a couple of points for legal:
- Indemnity/IP: we can accept third-party IP indemnity for claims arising from CrossCloud deliverables, but need to limit exposure for bundled open-source (can we list OSS modules to carve out?).
- Liability cap: commercial preference is <= 2x fees or $2M (whichever is higher) for standard partnerships. We can consider a higher cap tied to SOW value for a 12-month ramp period — will need a written business justification.
- Audit / log access: acceptable if scope is limited to specific systems and schedules (annual, 48-hour notice), and access is for troubleshooting only; we cannot provide full production PII exports.

Next steps I propose:
1) CrossCloud delivers one-page matrix mapping your requested clause -> proposed Redwood position (e.g., Indemnity: CrossCloud asks X; Redwood proposes Y).
2) We sync legal (30m) Thu 7/3 at 10:30 PT if that works — Vanessa and Marissa will join.
3) If we have alignment, Redwood will issue a term sheet and initial SOW and confirm PO vs DocuSign flow.

Procurement note: if CrossCloud needs PO-first, flag the estimated monthly run-rate and contract term so procurement can confirm internal approval path.

Thanks — we want to keep this light and avoid protracted back-and-forth.

Rishi
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jul 2025 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: RE: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization

Team — quick guidance from legal before the Thu sync:

Negotiation guardrails (approve for Rishi to accept within these bounds):
- Liability cap: up to $2,000,000 or 2x total fees incurred in prior 12 months, whichever is greater. Any ask above this requires VP approval and documented business case.
- Indemnity: accept limited third-party IP indemnity tied to CrossCloud deliverables; open-source carve-outs must be itemized.
- Audit: accept one scheduled read-only security assessment per year + scoped log access for troubleshooting (48-hour notice). No live forensics or source code access.
- Data residency / DPA: accept DPA track changes provided they include standard Redwood processor terms and SOC 2 attestation frequency; require SCCs for EU processing.
- Subprocessors: require notification + right to object for high-risk subprocessors; share DPIA if requested.
- Signature flow: Redwood prefers DocuSign; if CrossCloud mandates PO-first we can accept PO but must follow with DocuSign signature within 30 days.

Rishi — you have permission to accept the above during the call if CrossCloud is within bounds. If they push broader indemnity or unscoped audits, escalate to me.

V.
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships Operations
Redwood Inference

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CrossCloud partnership: MSA / DPA / SOW clause harmonization

Rishi / Vanessa —

Thanks for the sync this morning. We can live with the guardrails Vanessa outlined. A few confirmations from our side:
- We'll itemize OSS components to speed the IP carve-out.
- Audit: annual assessment + scoped log access (48-hr notice) acceptable.
- Liability cap: we'll accept the $2M / 2x fees cap for the initial SOW term.

Procurement will issue a short-form PO to cover the first 3 months while legal completes the DocuSign flow — attached is a signed term sheet and the PO will follow. Please send the DocuSign envelope for final signature and the SOW template so we can populate milestones.

Attachments: Signed_Term_Sheet.pdf
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef123456

Look forward to getting the integration live.

—Jared
